caption: Two friends sit in the back seat of a car, chatting, when the car brakes hard and both of them are thrown forward against their seat belts.
expectation: The lurch happens at the moment of braking, not before or after; it is forward, not backward or sideways; they settle back once the car has stopped.

caption: A woman standing in the aisle of a bus holding the overhead rail sways backward as the bus pulls away from the stop.
expectation: The sway is toward the rear of the bus and coincides with the bus starting to move; she steadies herself once the bus is moving at a steady speed.

caption: A full cup of coffee sits in the cup holder of a car, and as the car turns sharply left the coffee sloshes up the right side of the cup and spills over the rim.
expectation: The slosh is toward the outside of the turn (the right), begins as the turn begins, and the surface settles level again once the car straightens.

caption: A child gives a shopping cart a push across an empty parking lot and lets go, and the cart rolls on by itself until it slows to a stop.
expectation: The cart keeps a straight line after release, slows gradually rather than stopping the instant the hands leave it, and does not speed up or change direction on its own.

caption: A parent gives a child on a playground swing one push and steps back, and the swing keeps going back and forth on its own before gradually dying down.
expectation: Each arc is a little smaller than the last; the swing never rises higher than the pushed arc and does not stop at once.

caption: A woman is jogging on a treadmill when the belt stops abruptly, and she lurches forward and grabs the handrails.
expectation: The lurch happens the instant the belt stops, not before; it is forward, in the direction she was running, not backward or sideways; she catches herself on the rails and settles, and does not keep gliding forward after the belt is still.

caption: A phone lying flat on the dashboard of a car slides forward toward the windshield when the driver brakes suddenly at a red light.
expectation: The slide begins as the braking begins and is toward the front of the car; the phone stops when the car stops or when it hits the windshield.

caption: A boy takes a short run-up on a field, leaps forward off one foot, and after landing on both feet takes a few stumbling steps forward before he stops.
expectation: He leaves the ground going forward and comes down along a forward arc; the stumbling steps begin at the instant of landing and go the same way he was travelling, never backward or sideways; he does not hover at the top, and he does not stop dead on the spot the moment his feet touch.

caption: A waiter carrying a tray of full water glasses stops abruptly to avoid a running child, and the water sloshes forward and spills.
expectation: The water surges toward the direction the waiter was walking, at the moment he stops; the glasses may slide forward on the tray; the water settles afterwards.

caption: A ceiling fan running at full speed is switched off at the wall, and the blades keep turning for a while before coming to a stop.
expectation: The slowing is gradual over several seconds; the blades do not halt instantly, reverse, or speed up after the switch.

caption: An adult pulling a toddler in a wagon stops walking suddenly, and the wagon rolls on a little and the toddler tips forward in the seat.
expectation: The wagon does not stop the instant the adult does; it rolls until the handle checks it; the toddler tips forward, not backward.

caption: A bowler releases the ball at the top of the lane and it rolls the full length of the lane to the pins at the far end.
expectation: The ball keeps nearly constant speed along a straight or gently curving path and does not slow to a stop or wander before reaching the pins.

caption: A skateboarder riding along a sidewalk hits a raised crack, the board stops dead, and the rider is thrown forward off the board.
expectation: The rider continues in the direction of travel and stumbles or falls ahead of the stopped board; the rider does not stop with the board.

caption: A dog sprints across a smooth kitchen floor toward its food bowl, tries to stop in front of it, and skids past the bowl.
expectation: The paws slide on the floor while the dog keeps moving in its original direction; it comes to rest beyond or against the bowl, not on the spot.

caption: A spinning top is set going on a wooden table and left alone; it spins for a while, starts to wobble, and finally topples over.
expectation: The spin slows gradually and the wobble grows before the fall; the top does not speed up, right itself, or stop upright.

caption: A man shakes out a wet umbrella with a quick flick and stops his arm short, and the water drops fly off the tip and keep going in the direction of the flick.
expectation: The drops leave at the moment the umbrella stops, not before the flick or long after; they travel the way the tip was moving and then drop toward the ground; they do not hang beside the umbrella, follow it back, or scatter in every direction.

caption: A family sits in the back seat of a car as it takes a sharp bend on a country road, and all of them lean toward the outside of the bend.
expectation: The lean begins as the car enters the bend and eases as the road straightens; everyone leans the same way, away from the centre of the curve; nobody leans into the bend, and nobody moves before the car starts turning.

caption: A woman carrying groceries loses her grip on a bag of oranges at the top of a staircase, and the oranges tumble down the stairs to the bottom.
expectation: The oranges bounce from step to step and gather at the bottom; none stay in the air, roll upward, or stop on a step without reason.

caption: A man on a ladder hands a hammer down to a helper, the helper misses it, and the hammer falls to the ground.
expectation: The hammer drops straight down past the helper's hands, speeding up as it falls, and hits the ground; it does not pause or drift sideways.

caption: A cat nudges a pen off the edge of a desk with its paw and the pen falls to the floor.
expectation: The pen tips and falls as soon as it is past the edge; it does not hang in the air beyond the desk or drift.

caption: A child lets go of a helium balloon on a string in a park and the balloon floats up into the sky.
expectation: The balloon rises steadily with the string trailing below it; it does not fall, hover at hand height, or rise faster than a gentle drift.

caption: Autumn leaves come loose from a tree on a still afternoon and drift down to settle on the lawn.
expectation: The leaves fall slowly, fluttering and tumbling, always ending lower than they started; none rise again or hang still in the air.

caption: A waiter's hand slips, a ceramic plate drops from waist height onto a tiled restaurant floor, and it shatters.
expectation: The plate falls straight down and breaks on contact with the tile, pieces scattering outward; it does not bounce whole or break before it lands.

caption: A boy tosses a tennis ball straight up in his backyard and it comes back down into his open hands.
expectation: The ball slows as it rises, pauses for an instant at the top, and descends along nearly the same line, speeding up as it falls.

caption: A gardener turns a watering can upside down over a flower bed and the water pours out onto the soil.
expectation: The water falls from the spout straight down onto the soil in a stream; none stays in the can or flows upward.

caption: A stack of coins on the corner of a kitchen counter is knocked off by someone's elbow and the coins scatter on the floor.
expectation: The coins separate as they fall and land spread around the spot below the counter; the same coins that left the counter arrive on the floor.

caption: A cook cracks an egg on the rim of a bowl, pulls the shell apart above it, and the yolk and white drop into the bowl.
expectation: The contents fall straight down out of the shell as soon as it opens and do not remain suspended between the shell halves.

caption: A skydiver steps out of the open door of an airplane and drops away below it.
expectation: The skydiver falls faster at first while the plane moves on ahead; the skydiver does not stay level with the door or rise.

caption: A diver stands at the end of a high platform, bends her knees, jumps off, and falls into the pool.
expectation: She rises briefly then falls faster and faster until she enters the water; she does not slow before entry or hang in the air.

caption: A boy drops a water balloon from a second-floor balcony, and it falls straight down and bursts on the pavement.
expectation: The balloon starts falling the moment his hand opens, drops straight down and gets faster as it goes, and does not drift sideways, slow, or hover; it bursts only when it hits the pavement, and the water spreads out on the ground and stays there.

caption: A man presses a button on a vending machine, and a can drops inside the machine and lands in the tray at the bottom.
expectation: The can starts to fall only after the button is pressed, drops straight down behind the glass without pausing or drifting sideways, and comes to rest in the tray; one can leaves the shelf and the same one arrives below, with no can appearing from nowhere, vanishing on the way, or rising back up.

caption: A toddler on a beach lifts a handful of dry sand, opens her fingers, and the sand streams down onto the beach.
expectation: The sand runs straight down between her fingers and piles up below her hand; it does not hang in the air or blow away on a still day.

caption: A picture frame hanging on a wall comes loose from its nail and falls to the floor.
expectation: The frame slides or tips off the nail and drops down along the wall; it does not stay on the wall with nothing holding it or drift outward.

caption: A white cue ball rolls straight into a red ball sitting still on a pool table; the red ball rolls away and the cue ball stops.
expectation: The red ball sets off in the direction the cue ball was travelling at the instant of contact; the cue ball loses almost all its speed; the balls do not overlap.

caption: A bowling ball reaches the end of the lane, hits the front pin of a full rack, and the pins fly and scatter.
expectation: Pins move only after being struck by the ball or another pin, fly back and sideways, and the ball continues into the pit slowed; no pin is passed through.

caption: Two children in bumper cars drive straight at each other, meet head-on, and both cars bounce back a little.
expectation: Both cars stop or rebound at the moment of contact and the children are jolted forward in their seats; neither car passes through the other.

caption: A tennis ball is thrown hard against a brick wall and bounces back toward the thrower.
expectation: The ball flattens briefly at the wall and rebounds somewhat slower than it arrived; it does not stick, pause on the wall, or pass into it.

caption: A shopping cart rolls across a parking lot, runs into a concrete curb, and stops abruptly.
expectation: The cart stops at the curb with its front wheels jammed against it and may tip forward slightly; it does not roll through or over the curb.

caption: A finger tips over the first domino in a long row standing on a table, and the whole row falls one after another.
expectation: Each domino falls only after the previous one strikes it, the wave running steadily down the row; none fall early and none stand back up.

caption: A soccer ball kicked hard hits the goalpost squarely and rebounds back onto the field.
expectation: The rebound starts at the instant of contact; the post does not move or bend and the ball does not pass through it.

caption: A car in a parking lot rolls slowly forward, bumps into the back of a parked car, and stops.
expectation: The rolling car stops at the bumper and the parked car rocks or is nudged forward a little; neither car deforms much at this speed and neither passes into the other.

caption: A dodgeball hits a boy in the chest during a gym game, bounces off him, and drops to the floor.
expectation: The boy is pushed back a step at the moment of impact; the ball rebounds and falls nearby, not passing through him or sticking to him.

caption: A hockey puck slides along the ice, hits the metal goalpost, and deflects off at an angle.
expectation: The deflection happens at contact and the puck continues sliding in its new direction; the post stays fixed.

caption: A toy train runs along a track, hits a wooden block someone has placed across the rails, and stops.
expectation: The train stops or derails at the block and may push it a little; it does not pass through the block or stop before reaching it.

caption: A golfer putts a ball, it hits the back of the cup's rim, pops up, and drops into the hole.
expectation: The pop-up happens at the rim, the ball falls back into the hole under gravity, and it does not continue rolling as if the hole were not there.

caption: A curling stone glides down the ice, strikes another stone sitting in the house, and knocks it away while itself slowing to a stop.
expectation: The struck stone moves off at contact in roughly the direction of the hit; the moving stone loses most of its speed; the stones do not overlap.

caption: Two people walking around a corner in an office hallway bump shoulders and are both knocked a step sideways.
expectation: Both are pushed apart at the moment of contact and pause; their bodies do not overlap or pass through each other.

caption: A ping-pong ball served across the table clips the edge of the receiver's paddle and flies off sideways.
expectation: The change of direction happens at the paddle, the ball keeps moving after contact and comes down somewhere in the room; it does not stop dead in the air.

caption: A basketball thrown from the free-throw line hits the front of the rim, bounces up, and falls to the floor.
expectation: The bounce begins at the rim, the ball goes up or outward and then falls under gravity; it does not hover at the rim or pass through it.

caption: A child rolls a beach ball across the sand into an upright plastic bucket, and the ball stops while the bucket is nudged over.
expectation: The bucket moves only when the ball reaches it; the light ball stops or rolls back a little; the ball does not pass through the bucket.

caption: A child on a sled slides down a snowy slope, runs out onto a flat patch of bare grass, and stops within a short distance.
expectation: The slowing begins where the snow ends and is much sharper on grass than it was on snow; the sled does not keep gliding or stop while still on snow.

caption: A rubber ball rolls across a polished wooden floor onto a thick shaggy rug and comes to a stop on the rug.
expectation: The ball rolls freely on the wood and slows noticeably only once it reaches the rug; it does not stop on the wood or speed up on the rug.

caption: A driver tries to pull away from a snow-covered kerb, the car's rear wheels spin in place and throw up snow, and the car stays almost where it is.
expectation: The wheels turn fast while the car creeps forward only a little and never surges ahead as it would on a dry road; the snow is flung backward from the spinning wheels, not forward or upward from nowhere; the car does not move while the wheels are still, and the wheels do not stop spinning while the car keeps gaining speed.

caption: A woman in smooth-soled shoes steps onto a patch of ice on a sidewalk, her foot slides forward, and she stumbles.
expectation: The slip happens as the foot lands on the ice, not before; her arms come up to balance; her foot grips normally on the pavement before and after.

caption: A coin is set spinning on its edge on a wooden table, wobbles, and falls flat.
expectation: The spin slows and the wobble widens before the coin clatters flat; it does not speed up, right itself, or stop upright.

caption: A boy rolls a hula hoop along a sidewalk and lets it go; it rolls on by itself, wobbles, and falls over.
expectation: The hoop stays upright while fast, leans more as it slows, and falls onto its side; it does not fall while still rolling fast or stand still upright.

caption: A car tire stood on its tread is pushed along a level driveway; it rolls a long way, wobbles, and topples flat.
expectation: The roll slows gradually and the topple comes only once the tire is slow; it does not stop abruptly or fall while rolling fast.

caption: A wheeled suitcase pulled from a smooth airport floor onto a cobblestone street starts bumping and rattling over the stones.
expectation: The wheels roll smoothly on the floor and jolt over each stone on the cobbles; the change happens exactly at the edge between surfaces.

caption: A teacher draws a large circle on a blackboard with a piece of chalk, and a white line appears where the chalk has passed.
expectation: The line grows only at the chalk tip and only while the chalk touches the board; nothing appears ahead of the tip or where the chalk is lifted off; the part already drawn stays put and does not fade, shift or vanish; the shape on the board matches the path the hand traced.

caption: A man rolls a heavy wooden barrel up a plank onto a truck bed, lets go halfway up, and the barrel rolls back down to the ground.
expectation: The roll back begins as soon as he lets go and speeds up down the plank; the barrel does not stay put on the slope or continue upward.

caption: A bicycle is turned upside down, someone spins the front wheel by hand and steps back, and the wheel keeps spinning for a while before stopping.
expectation: The spin slows gradually and evenly; the wheel does not stop at once, speed up, or reverse.

caption: A child rolls a ball up a gentle grassy slope; it slows, stops, and rolls back down toward the child.
expectation: The ball slows steadily on the way up, pauses for an instant, and comes back along roughly the same line, speeding up on the way down.

caption: A wheelbarrow full of soil is pushed across a soft lawn, where its wheel sinks and drags, and then onto a paved patio, where it rolls easily.
expectation: The wheel leaves a track in the lawn and rolls without sinking on the patio; the change happens at the edge of the paving.

caption: A log is rolled off the back of a trailer onto a slight downhill slope and rolls down to the bottom.
expectation: The log turns about its length as it rolls, speeds up on the slope, and comes to rest at the bottom or against an obstacle; it does not stop on the slope or roll uphill.

caption: A skateboarder rolling along a flat path lowers his back foot and drags it on the ground, and the board slows and comes to a stop.
expectation: The slowing starts the moment the foot touches the ground, not before and not long after; the board keeps a straight line as it slows and stops without a jolt, with the rider still standing on it; it does not keep rolling at full speed while the foot drags, and does not speed up or roll backward.

caption: A car drives onto a frozen pond, the driver turns the steering wheel sharply, and the car keeps sliding straight ahead instead of turning.
expectation: The car's path barely changes even though the wheels point sideways; the rear may swing out; the car does not turn crisply as on dry road.

caption: A father tosses a soft ball across the lawn to his daughter, who stands with her arms out, and the ball lands in her arms.
expectation: The ball follows a smooth arc, rising then falling; it does not fly straight, hang in the air, or change direction midway.

caption: A gardener points a running hose upward at an angle over a vegetable bed and the water comes down on the far side of the bed.
expectation: The stream leaves the nozzle and curves over in an arc before reaching the ground; it does not travel in a straight line or stop in the air.

caption: A teenager shoots a basketball from the three-point line and it drops through the hoop.
expectation: The ball rises in an arc, peaks, and descends into the hoop; it does not travel flat or hover above the rim.

caption: A child on a moving swing lets go at the front of the arc, flies forward, and lands on the ground ahead of the swing.
expectation: The child leaves the seat with the swing's forward motion and follows a curve down to the ground; the empty swing keeps swinging.

caption: A boy throws a flat stone sideways low over a calm lake, and it skips across the surface several times before sinking.
expectation: Each hop is shorter and lower than the last and leaves a ring of ripples; the stone finally sinks and does not float or skip forever.

caption: A lawn sprinkler sends jets of water up and out over a garden, and the water falls onto the grass some distance away.
expectation: Each jet rises, curves over, and descends; the water lands at a distance that matches how high it was thrown and does not stay up.

caption: A batter connects with a pitch, sends the baseball high into the outfield, and it comes down into a fielder's glove.
expectation: The ball climbs in a long arc, slows near the top, and falls steadily; it does not level off or drop straight down.

caption: A snowball thrown across a snowy yard hits a friend on the shoulder and bursts into loose snow.
expectation: The snowball arcs through the air, breaks apart on impact rather than bouncing off whole, and snow scatters and falls.

caption: A frog on a lily pad leaps toward the bank of a pond and lands on it.
expectation: The frog rises and comes down in an arc; the lily pad dips and bobs as it pushes off; the frog does not hover or change direction mid-air.

caption: A jogger comes to a wide puddle on a path, jumps over it, and lands on the far side.
expectation: The jogger follows a shallow arc from take-off to landing with no hang time; the legs come forward for the landing.

caption: A referee flips a coin into the air at the start of a match and catches it as it comes down.
expectation: The coin spins as it rises, slows to a peak, and falls back to the hand; it does not hover at the top.

caption: A man throws a dart at a dartboard on a pub wall and it sticks in the board.
expectation: The dart flies point-first in a slight arc and stops dead on impact with its tip in the board; it does not pass through the board or float.

caption: A horse and rider gallop toward a low fence, jump over it, and land on the far side.
expectation: The horse leaves the ground before the fence, arcs over it, lands front legs first, and continues forward; it does not hover above the fence.

caption: A goalkeeper punts a soccer ball far down the field, and it lands and bounces near the far end.
expectation: The ball soars in a high arc and descends steadily; on landing it bounces lower than its flight height and rolls.

caption: A dolphin swimming fast bursts out of the sea, arcs through the air, and splashes back in.
expectation: The dolphin rises, slows at the top, and falls back into the water; it does not stay suspended above the surface or change direction mid-air.

caption: A kid drops a rubber ball from shoulder height onto a concrete driveway and it bounces several times before rolling away.
expectation: Each bounce is lower than the one before and none is higher than the drop height; the bounces get quicker as they get smaller.

caption: A mover pushes against the side of a tall stack of cardboard boxes in a hallway and the stack topples, boxes tumbling to the floor.
expectation: The stack leans away from the push before falling; the upper boxes go first and fall on the side away from the mover; they do not float or fall toward him.

caption: A girl pulls a block out of the bottom row of a tall wooden block tower and the tower collapses.
expectation: The collapse starts as the support is removed, the tower sways then falls, and the blocks scatter on the table; it does not stand for long on nothing.

caption: A bicycle resting on its kickstand is bumped by a passing pedestrian and falls over onto its side.
expectation: The bike rocks, leans further, and hits the ground; it falls on the side away from the kickstand's support and does not right itself.

caption: A man sitting in a dining chair leans back until only the two rear legs are on the floor, leans a little further, and tips over backward with the chair.
expectation: The fall begins once he leans past the balance point and speeds up; he and the chair land on the floor behind him; the chair does not hang balanced.

caption: A toddler stacks plastic cups into a tower on a carpet, bats the top cup with his hand, and the top of the tower falls.
expectation: The struck cup flies off in the direction of the swipe, the cups below wobble and some fall; cups do not float or fall before being disturbed.

caption: A waiter's elbow knocks a full wine glass on a table; it tips over and the wine spills across the tablecloth.
expectation: The glass falls in the direction it was knocked, the wine pours out as it goes over and spreads on the cloth; the glass does not swing back upright.

caption: A stepladder standing on a lawn is pushed sideways by a man, who then steps away, and the ladder falls over onto the grass.
expectation: The ladder leans in the direction of the push and falls that way, speeding up; it does not stay leaning in the air with nothing holding it.

caption: A child taps the tall thin tower on top of a sandcastle with a shovel, and the tower crumbles and slides down the side of the castle.
expectation: The sand breaks into loose grains and clumps that fall downward; the tower does not tip over as a rigid piece or stay standing.

caption: A snowman's head is knocked sideways by a thrown snowball, rolls off the body, and drops to the snow.
expectation: The head moves at the moment of impact in the direction of the throw, falls to the ground, and may break apart; it does not hover above the shoulders.

caption: A pyramid of empty soda cans at a carnival booth is hit by a tennis ball, and the cans fly off and fall to the counter.
expectation: The struck cans fly backward first, the cans above them lose support and fall; cans move only after being hit or losing support.

caption: Two children sit on opposite ends of a seesaw; one slides off her seat and the other child's end drops to the ground.
expectation: The drop happens as soon as the girl's weight leaves the seat; the empty end rises at the same time; the beam does not stay level.

caption: A boy slowly pushes a hardback book toward the edge of a table until it tips over the edge and falls to the floor.
expectation: The book stays flat and still on the table while most of it is still supported; it tips only once most of its length is past the edge, turning over the edge as it goes and landing below it; it does not fall while barely overhanging, hang far out over the edge without tipping, drift off flat without turning, or float.

caption: A student balances a stack of textbooks on the palm of one hand, tilts the hand to one side, and the books slide off and fall to the floor.
expectation: The books slide toward the low side of the hand and fall from there; they do not stay on the tilted palm or fall toward the high side.

caption: A cyclist comes to a stop at a light with both feet still on the pedals, the bicycle leans to one side, and cyclist and bike fall over together.
expectation: The lean grows steadily into a fall toward the low side; the bike does not stay upright unsupported or fall toward the high side.

caption: A cook balances a wooden spoon across the rim of a pot, sets a heavy ladle on one end, and the spoon tips and the ladle falls into the pot.
expectation: The weighted end goes down as soon as the ladle is set on it; the spoon tips off the rim; nothing stays balanced on nothing.

caption: A person carrying a stack of dinner plates in one hand trips on a rug, and the plates slide off and shatter on the floor.
expectation: The plates leave the hand as the person stumbles, fall to the floor, and break on impact; they do not break in the air or float.

caption: A child climbs an unanchored bookshelf and pulls on the top; the shelf tips forward and falls, spilling books.
expectation: The shelf leans toward the child, the books slide off the shelves as it tilts, and it falls to the floor; it does not fall backward or stop mid-tilt.

caption: Two teams pick up a slack rope lying on the grass and begin a tug of war; the rope goes taut and the middle marker moves toward the stronger side.
expectation: The rope straightens between the teams before anyone moves, bows only where hands grip it, and stays taut while they pull.

caption: A large dog on a leash spots a squirrel and lunges after it; the leash snaps taut, the dog is stopped short, and the owner is jerked forward a step.
expectation: The leash goes from slack to straight at the instant the dog reaches its end; the dog stops and the owner moves at that same instant, not before.

caption: A woman hangs a basket of wet laundry from the middle of a clothesline strung between two posts, and the line sags under the weight.
expectation: The sag forms as the basket is hung, is deepest at the basket, and the line stays straight between basket and posts; it does not stay level.

caption: A child holds a kite string as a steady wind lifts the kite, and the string pulls taut from her hand up to the kite.
expectation: The string runs in a shallow taut curve and tugs at her hand; it does not hang slack while the kite is flying.

caption: A man lowers a bucket into a well on a rope and hauls it back up full of water.
expectation: The rope hangs straight down under the bucket's weight and stays taut as he pulls; the bucket rises only as fast as rope is pulled in.

caption: A man sits down in an empty hammock strung between two trees, and the hammock sags deeply under him.
expectation: The sag forms as his weight lands, the ropes pull straight to the trees, and the hammock swings gently before settling.

caption: A truck backs up until the tow rope to a stuck car lies slack on the ground, then drives forward; the rope goes taut and the car jerks into motion behind it.
expectation: The car does not move until the rope has straightened; the jerk happens at the instant the rope goes tight.

caption: An angler's fishing line goes tight as a fish takes the bait, and the rod bends toward the water.
expectation: The bend appears as the line tightens and points toward where the line enters the water; the rod straightens if the line goes slack.

caption: A child sits on a rope swing, a friend gives her a push, and she swings back and forth beneath the branch.
expectation: The ropes stay straight and taut throughout and the seat follows an arc under the branch; the ropes do not go slack or bend.

caption: A parent pulls a sled with a child on it across a snowy field by a rope, then stops, and the rope goes slack.
expectation: The rope is taut while the sled is being pulled and droops only after the parent stops; the sled slides on a little before stopping.

caption: A cat pounces onto a spider web strung between two garden plants and the web tears apart under it.
expectation: The strands stretch and break at the moment the cat lands, clinging to its fur; the web does not hold the cat up.

caption: A boat tied to a dock by a long line drifts away on the tide until the line goes taut and stops it.
expectation: The boat moves freely while the line is slack and stops the instant the line straightens, then swings on the end of the line.

caption: A crane cable is hooked to a steel beam lying on the ground; the operator lifts, the cable tightens, and the beam rises off the ground.
expectation: The cable straightens first and the beam leaves the ground only after that, hanging straight below the hook; it does not rise before the cable is tight.

caption: A woman wrings out a soaked towel over a sink with both hands, and water streams out of it.
expectation: The towel twists thinner where wrung and the water falls straight down into the sink while she twists; the flow stops when she stops.

caption: A necklace catches on a door handle as a woman walks past; the chain goes tight and jerks her head back.
expectation: The jerk happens at the instant the chain goes taut; the chain does not stretch like elastic; it either holds or snaps.

caption: A man pulls the rope on a flagpole hand over hand, and the flag rises up the pole as the rope runs through the pulley at the top.
expectation: The rope stays taut on the pulled side, the flag moves only as fast as rope is pulled in, and it stops rising when he stops; the rope does not stretch or go slack while lifting.

caption: A child grabs the handle of a backyard zip line and rides it down to the far end, the cable sagging under her weight.
expectation: The cable dips most under the handle and the dip travels with her; the cable stays straight on either side of her and does not go slack or stretch like elastic.

caption: A hand squeezes a wet kitchen sponge over a sink, water streams out, and the sponge springs back to shape when the hand opens.
expectation: The sponge compresses only while squeezed and the water runs out during the squeeze; the recovery is quick and nearly complete.

caption: A man steps on an empty aluminum soda can lying on a driveway and it crumples flat and stays flat.
expectation: The crushing happens under his foot, not before; the can keeps its crushed shape after he lifts his foot and does not spring back.

caption: A child presses both thumbs into a ball of modelling clay on a table, and the clay keeps the thumbprints after the hands lift away.
expectation: The clay dents where pressed and bulges beside the thumbs; the prints stay and the ball does not pop back into a sphere.

caption: A woman pushes down on a foam pillow with one hand, lifts the hand away, and the pillow puffs back to its shape.
expectation: The pillow sinks only under the hand and recovers gradually after release; it does not stay dented or spring back instantly like rubber.

caption: A boy jumps onto the middle of a bed, the mattress dips under him, and he bounces slightly before settling.
expectation: The dip appears as he lands and the rebound is smaller than the drop; the bed does not stay rigid like a floor or throw him higher than he came from.

caption: A man bends a metal paper clip open with his fingers, lets go, and the clip stays in its new shape.
expectation: The bending happens only where his fingers act, and the clip does not spring closed after release.

caption: A child presses a hand into a slab of memory foam, lifts it away, and the hand-shaped dent slowly fills back in.
expectation: The dent matches the hand and persists for a few seconds before disappearing gradually; it does not vanish instantly or stay permanently.

caption: A man squeezes an inflated balloon between his palms; it flattens between his hands and bulges out at the sides, then rounds out again when he lets go.
expectation: The balloon keeps roughly the same overall size while squeezed, bulging where it is not pressed; it does not shrink, pass through his hands, or stay flat.

caption: A child packs loose snow between mittened hands into a firm snowball that holds its shape when the hands open.
expectation: The snow compresses and sticks together under pressure; the ball stays a ball after release and does not fall apart into loose snow or spring back.

caption: A gymnast lands feet-first in the centre of a trampoline, the mat stretches deep under her, and it throws her back up into the air.
expectation: The mat dips as she lands and springs back as she rises; the rebound follows the dip, and she leaves the mat as it returns to flat.

caption: A tennis racket strikes a ball hard during a serve and the ball flies off toward the far court.
expectation: The ball flattens against the strings for an instant and leaves round again; it does not pass through the strings or stick to them.

caption: A baker presses the heel of her hand into a ball of bread dough on a floured counter and the dough flattens and spreads.
expectation: The dough deforms only where pressed and slowly keeps the pressed shape; it does not spring back like rubber or crack like clay.

caption: A person sits down on a large cardboard box in a garage, the box caves in under them, and it stays crumpled when they stand up.
expectation: The top folds in and the sides buckle as the weight lands; the box does not hold like a stool or spring back to shape.

caption: A child bends a fresh green twig into a curve, lets go of one end, and the twig springs back to nearly straight.
expectation: The twig bends smoothly without snapping and straightens on release; it does not stay curved or break.

caption: A cook presses a ripe avocado firmly between finger and thumb and the skin dents inward and stays dented.
expectation: The dent forms under the fingers and remains after they lift; the avocado does not spring back like a ball or crack like a shell.

caption: An archer draws a bowstring back to her cheek and releases it, and the arrow flies off toward the target.
expectation: The bow limbs flex as she draws and spring back on release; the arrow leaves at the instant of release, not before.

caption: A child stretches a rubber band between two fingers and lets one end slip; the band snaps back and drops.
expectation: The band flies toward the finger still holding it at the instant of release and returns to its unstretched size.

caption: A child cuts a sheet of coloured paper in half with scissors, and the two halves fall apart on the table.
expectation: The paper parts exactly where and when the blades close, leaving straight edges; it is not cut ahead of the blades and the halves do not rejoin.

caption: A man tears a loaf of crusty bread in two with his hands at a dinner table.
expectation: The crust cracks and the loaf pulls apart with a ragged tear where his hands pull, crumbs falling; the two pieces stay separate.

caption: A cook slices a ripe tomato into rounds on a cutting board with a sharp knife.
expectation: Each stroke separates one slice that falls or is pushed aside, juice and seeds leak onto the board, and the tomato gets shorter; it is not cut ahead of the blade.

caption: A woman rips a strip of packing tape off a cardboard box and the box flaps come free.
expectation: The tape peels up along its length as she pulls, sometimes taking the top layer of cardboard with it; the flaps open only after the tape is off.

caption: A boy bites into a whole apple and takes a bite-shaped piece out of it.
expectation: The hollow appears exactly where he bit and stays there; the apple does not grow back or show the bite before his teeth reach it.

caption: A chef chops a carrot into rounds with quick knife strokes, and the pieces pile up beside the blade.
expectation: Each stroke severs one round, the carrot gets shorter as pieces come off, and the number of pieces matches the number of cuts.

caption: A tailor tears a length of cotton fabric along a snipped edge, and the fabric rips into two pieces.
expectation: The rip runs in a straight line following the weave as she pulls, loose threads fraying at the edges; the tear does not run ahead of the pull.

caption: A child pulls a tuft of cotton candy off the top of a cone and it comes away as a separate wisp.
expectation: The floss stretches into strands before parting and leaves a ragged surface on the cone; the tuft does not rejoin the cone.

caption: A hiker snaps a dry twig in half between her hands with a crack.
expectation: The twig bends only slightly before breaking into two pieces with splintered ends; it does not bend like rubber or rejoin.

caption: A woman breaks a bar of chocolate along its grooves into separate pieces.
expectation: The bar snaps cleanly along the grooves where she bends it; the pieces do not stick back together or bend without breaking.

caption: A teenager pulls the two sides of a bag of chips apart at the top seam and the bag pops open.
expectation: The seal gives way suddenly as she pulls, sometimes tearing down one side, and the chips inside are visible; the bag does not open before the pull.

caption: A host cuts a slice out of a round birthday cake and lifts it onto a plate, leaving a wedge-shaped gap in the cake.
expectation: The gap matches the slice that was removed and stays open; the cake does not close up after the slice is lifted away.

caption: A man peels an orange with his thumbs, starting from a slit at the top, and the pieces of peel pile up beside the bare fruit.
expectation: The peel comes away only where his thumbs work, exposing the segments underneath; the fruit does not regrow its skin.

caption: A man swings an axe down onto a log standing on end on a chopping block, and the log splits into two pieces that fall apart to the sides.
expectation: The split starts where the blade bites and runs down the log; the halves fall away only after the blow lands; the axe does not pass through without effect.

caption: A student tears a page out of a spiral notebook, leaving a fringe of paper on the coil.
expectation: The page rips along the perforated edge as it is pulled and becomes a separate sheet; the notebook does not regain the page.

caption: A gardener cuts through a thick garden hose with a pair of shears, leaving two open ends.
expectation: The hose is pinched and then severed where the blades close; the cut does not appear elsewhere on the hose or before the blades meet.

caption: A boy pulls a stubborn weed out of the soil by its leaves, and the whole plant comes up with its roots and clinging soil.
expectation: The soil around the stem lifts and breaks as the roots come free; the plant does not float out untouched or leave the ground undisturbed.

caption: A woman pours water from a jug into an empty drinking glass on a table until the glass is nearly full.
expectation: A continuous stream falls from the jug into the glass and the level rises steadily while the jug empties; the water does not vanish, flow upward, or appear in the glass before the stream reaches it.

caption: A child knocks over a full glass of milk on a kitchen table, and the milk spreads across the table and drips off the edge.
expectation: The milk flows out as the glass goes over, spreads in a widening puddle, and runs off the low edge in drips; it does not hold a glass shape or flow uphill.

caption: A boy drops a stone into a still garden pond; it splashes, sinks, and ripples spread out across the water.
expectation: The splash rises at the moment of entry, the rings spread outward from that spot and fade as they widen; the stone does not float.

caption: A cook pours olive oil into a glass of water, and the oil gathers in a layer floating on top of the water.
expectation: The oil sinks briefly in blobs and then rises to the surface; it does not mix in or settle at the bottom.

caption: A motorboat speeds across a calm lake, leaving a spreading wake behind it.
expectation: The wake is a V opening behind the boat with foam at the stern; the water ahead of the boat stays calm and the wake does not run ahead of the boat.

caption: A woman tips a jar of honey over a slice of toast, and the honey flows out in a slow thick ribbon onto the toast.
expectation: The ribbon is unbroken and falls straight down, piling up and spreading slowly on the toast; it does not pour thin and fast like water.

caption: A man tilts a half-full fish tank to one side while carrying it, and the water climbs the low side and spills over the rim.
expectation: The water surface stays level while the tank tilts; the spill comes from the low side only and starts when the rim reaches the surface.

caption: A child blows through a straw into a glass of soapy water, and bubbles rise and pile up in a foam at the top of the glass.
expectation: Bubbles form at the straw tip and rise; the foam builds while the child blows and spills over the rim if it gets tall enough; bubbles do not sink.

caption: A bartender drops several ice cubes into a glass of soda, and the cubes bob up and float near the surface.
expectation: The cubes splash, dip below, and come back up to float with their tops just above the surface; the soda level rises as they go in.

caption: A woman drops a dry sponge into a basin of water; it floats, darkens as it soaks up water, and settles lower.
expectation: The darkening spreads from the wet side and the sponge sinks gradually as it fills; it does not sink instantly like a stone or stay dry.

caption: A bucket of water is emptied over a concrete sidewalk, and the water spreads out in a thin sheet and runs toward the lower side.
expectation: The sheet spreads outward from where the water lands and flows downhill, leaving the concrete wet and dark; it does not stay in a heap or run uphill.

caption: A cook tips a saucepan and pours soup into a bowl until it is full and begins to spill over the sides.
expectation: The level rises steadily and the overflow begins exactly when it reaches the rim, running down the outside onto the counter.

caption: A dog climbs out of a lake and shakes itself, sending a spray of water droplets flying off its fur.
expectation: Droplets leave the fur in all directions during the shake and fall to the ground around the dog; they do not hang in the air or return to the fur.

caption: A woman paddles a kayak across a calm lake, pulling the blade back through the water, and the kayak moves forward.
expectation: The kayak moves the opposite way to the blade's pull and starts moving with the stroke, not before it; each stroke leaves a swirl in the water behind the blade; between strokes the kayak glides on and slows only gently; it never moves backward or sideways while she pulls, and from rest it does not move before the first stroke.

caption: A girl sucks on a straw standing in a glass of juice, and the juice climbs the straw into her mouth while the level in the glass goes down.
expectation: The juice rises inside the straw only while she sucks and drops back when she stops; the glass level falls as she drinks; juice does not leave the glass any other way.

caption: A cook squeezes a plastic ketchup bottle over a plate of fries, and ketchup comes out of the nozzle onto the fries.
expectation: Ketchup flows only while the bottle is squeezed, in a thick stream that falls onto the plate; the bottle dents where pressed and refills its shape when released.

caption: A boy pushes an inflated beach ball under the water in a swimming pool and lets go, and the ball pops back up to the surface.
expectation: The ball rises as soon as it is released, breaks the surface with a splash, bobs, and settles floating mostly above the water; it does not stay under or sink.

caption: A baker pours a bag of sugar into a large mixing bowl, and the sugar builds up into a mound in the bowl.
expectation: The sugar streams down in a steady flow and the mound grows as a cone that slumps at the sides; it does not pour as one solid lump or stack into a column.

caption: A child turns a bucket packed with damp sand upside down on the beach and lifts it off, leaving a bucket-shaped sand tower standing.
expectation: The tower keeps the bucket's shape with edges crumbling slightly as the bucket comes away; it does not slump into a heap or stay stuck in the bucket.

caption: A bag of rice slips off a kitchen counter, splits open on the floor, and rice grains scatter across the floor.
expectation: The grains spray outward from the split as the bag hits and spread into a wide scatter; they do not stay in a bag shape or bounce back into the bag.

caption: A diner shakes a salt shaker over a plate of fries and salt grains fall onto the fries.
expectation: Grains fall from the holes only during each shake and land on the fries and plate below; they do not hang in the air or fall upward.

caption: A dump truck tips its bed and unloads a pile of gravel onto a construction site, where it settles into a heap.
expectation: The gravel slides out in a rush as the bed tilts, spreads at the bottom, and forms a broad cone with sloping sides; it does not hold the bed's shape.

caption: An hourglass is turned over on a desk, and sand runs from the top chamber into the bottom one.
expectation: The sand runs in a thin steady stream through the neck, a cone building in the bottom while the top empties; the flow does not reverse or stop midway.

caption: A gardener empties a bag of soil into a flower pot, filling it with a loose heap.
expectation: The soil falls in clumps and crumbs and settles when the pot is tapped; it does not pour like liquid or hold the bag's shape.

caption: A man walks barefoot across a stretch of dry beach sand, leaving a trail of footprints behind him.
expectation: Each foot sinks a little and pushes sand up around the print; the prints appear only where he has stepped and stay behind him.

caption: A man shovels a heap of snow off a driveway onto the lawn, building a ragged pile there.
expectation: Each shovelful flies in a loose clump that breaks apart in the air and lands scattered; the driveway clears where he has shovelled.

caption: A cook pours dried beans from a bag into a glass jar until it is full and beans spill over onto the counter.
expectation: The beans fill the jar from the bottom up; the overflow begins when the jar is full and the extra beans bounce and roll on the counter.

caption: A farmer scatters a handful of seed across bare soil with a sweep of his arm, and the seeds land spread over a wide patch.
expectation: The seeds fan out through the air in an arc during the sweep and drop onto the soil; they do not hang in the air or land in a single spot.

caption: A barista knocks a used coffee filter against the rim of a bin, and the puck of wet grounds drops out and breaks apart in the bin.
expectation: The puck comes loose on the knock and falls straight down, breaking into clumps and crumbs as it lands; it does not float or stay in the filter.

caption: A child kicks the top of a small pile of dry sand in a sandbox, and sand sprays forward and leaves a gouge in the pile.
expectation: The spray goes in the direction of the kick and falls back to the ground a short way off; the pile does not move as one block.

caption: A worker pours a bucket of gravel slowly onto one spot on a flat concrete floor, and the gravel piles up into a cone.
expectation: The cone widens as it grows taller, stones rolling down its sides; it does not stack into a column or spread flat like water.

caption: A woman tips a box of dry pasta into a pot of boiling water, and the pasta sinks and settles at the bottom.
expectation: The pieces slide out and splash into the water, then sink; they do not float on the surface or hang in the water.

caption: A cat digs in a litter box with its front paws, flinging litter backward and leaving a hollow.
expectation: Litter is flung in small showers in the direction of the paw strokes and lands nearby; the hollow forms where the paws dig.

caption: A child drags a stick through a patch of loose gravel on a path, leaving a furrow behind it.
expectation: Small ridges of pushed-aside stones form on each side of the furrow as the stick moves; the furrow does not appear ahead of the stick or close up behind it.

caption: A boy blows up a balloon, lets go of the neck without tying it, and the balloon shoots off around the room until it drops limp to the floor.
expectation: The balloon flies erratically while air escapes and shrinks as it goes; it falls only once empty and does not reinflate.

caption: A gust of wind lifts a man's wide-brimmed hat off his head on a seafront and carries it away along the ground.
expectation: The hat moves in the same direction as other things blown by the wind, tumbling and skipping along; it does not move against the wind.

caption: A girl holds a dandelion clock up and blows hard on it, and the seeds detach and drift away.
expectation: The seeds leave in the direction of her breath and float slowly downward as they drift; the stalk is left bare and the seeds do not return.

caption: A desk fan is switched on next to a loose stack of papers, and the top sheets lift and scatter across the desk and floor.
expectation: The sheets move only after the fan starts and fly away from it; the bottom sheets stay longer than the top ones.

caption: A woman opens an umbrella on a windy street corner, and the wind tugs it sideways and flips the canopy inside out.
expectation: The umbrella leans downwind and pulls her arm; the flip happens when a gust catches the underside; the canopy does not return to shape on its own.

caption: Smoke rises from a house chimney on a calm winter evening and thins out as it climbs.
expectation: The column drifts upward and widens; it does not sink to the ground or gather back into the chimney.

caption: A child dips a wand in soap solution and blows a stream of bubbles in a park; the bubbles float away on the breeze and pop one by one.
expectation: The bubbles drift with the wind and sink slowly; each pops when it touches something or after a few seconds and does not re-form.

caption: A light curtain hanging in front of an open window billows into the room with each gust of wind and falls back between gusts.
expectation: The curtain moves in step with the wind, inward with a gust and back when it drops; it does not move on its own or against the wind.

caption: A woman aims a hairdryer at her long hair in front of a mirror, and her hair streams away from the nozzle.
expectation: The hair blows in the direction the dryer points and falls back when the dryer is moved away.

caption: A groundskeeper points a leaf blower at a pile of dry leaves on a path, and the leaves scatter and tumble away from the nozzle.
expectation: The leaves move away from the blower in the direction of the blast, some lifting into the air, and settle further along; they do not move toward it.

caption: A flag hanging limp from a pole outside a school lifts and streams out as a strong wind picks up.
expectation: The flag stretches out downwind and ripples along its length; it points the same way as other things blown by the wind.

caption: A plastic shopping bag lying on an empty parking lot inflates and tumbles away across the lot as the wind rises.
expectation: The bag moves downwind, rising and dipping with the gusts; it does not travel against the wind or move before the wind picks up.

caption: A man blows out the candles on a birthday cake with one breath, and thin wisps of smoke rise from the wicks.
expectation: The flames lean away from him and go out during the breath; the smoke rises upward; the candles do not relight on their own.

caption: A camper opens the valve of an inflated air mattress and presses down on it, and the mattress hisses and sags flat.
expectation: The mattress collapses most where it is pressed and stays flat; it does not reinflate on its own.

caption: A man works a hand pump attached to a flat bicycle tyre, and the tyre fills out until it is firm and round.
expectation: The tyre swells a little with each stroke and not between strokes; it does not inflate instantly or shrink while he pumps.

caption: A feather is dropped in front of a running box fan and is carried away by the airflow before drifting to the floor.
expectation: The feather moves away from the fan, tumbling, and lands some distance off rather than falling straight down; it does not rise indefinitely.

caption: A woman runs a vacuum cleaner nozzle over crumbs scattered on a carpet, and the crumbs disappear into the nozzle.
expectation: Crumbs jump toward the nozzle only when it comes close and vanish into it; the carpet is clean behind the nozzle's path; crumbs do not fly away from it.

caption: A woman walks along a city sidewalk carrying a handbag, one foot after the other.
expectation: One foot is on the ground at all times, the arms swing opposite to the legs, and the limbs bend only at hips, knees, elbows and shoulders.

caption: A man jogs across a park lawn from one side to the other.
expectation: Both feet leave the ground briefly between strides, the arms swing in rhythm, and the body bobs slightly with each step; legs alternate.

caption: A boy climbs a flight of stairs two at a time and reaches the top.
expectation: Each knee lifts high and the foot lands on top of a step, not inside it; the body rises with each push.

caption: An elderly man lowers himself into an armchair and sits down.
expectation: He bends at hips and knees and leans forward slightly as he sinks; his body does not fold anywhere other than at the joints.

caption: A dog runs across a yard, picks up a ball in its mouth, and runs back.
expectation: Its four legs move in a galloping rhythm and the body stretches and bunches with each bound; it keeps four legs and one tail throughout.

caption: A horse gallops across an open field from one end to the other.
expectation: The legs move in a galloping sequence with moments when all four hooves are off the ground, the mane and tail stream back, and the legs bend only at their joints.

caption: A cat crouches on a kitchen floor, jumps up onto the counter, and lands on it.
expectation: The cat pushes off with its hind legs, arcs upward, and lands front paws first; it does not float up or land before it has jumped.

caption: A woman bends down, picks up a heavy box from the floor, and straightens up holding it.
expectation: She bends her knees and back to reach the box, lifts with visible effort, and leans back slightly to balance the weight once standing.

caption: A boy catches a ball thrown to him with both hands and holds on to it.
expectation: His arms reach toward the ball, his hands close around it, and his arms give slightly as it arrives; the ball does not pass through his hands.

caption: A swimmer does front crawl across a pool and reaches the far wall.
expectation: The arms come over one at a time and pull through the water, the legs kick, and the head turns to breathe; each arm stays attached and bends only at elbow and shoulder.

caption: A girl rides a kick scooter along a path, pushing off the ground with one foot and gliding between pushes.
expectation: One foot stays on the board while the other kicks; the scooter speeds up on each kick and coasts between them.

caption: A man slips on a wet floor in a supermarket aisle and falls down.
expectation: His foot shoots forward, his arms fly up, and he goes down to the floor; his body stays in one piece and bends only at the joints.

caption: A couple dances a slow waltz around a living room, holding each other.
expectation: They step in time with their feet on the floor; their bodies stay separate and do not pass through one another or merge.

caption: A man struggles to twist the lid off a tight jar and finally gets it open, lid in hand.
expectation: His hands grip jar and lid and his forearms twist in opposite directions; the lid turns and comes off only after the twist, not before.

caption: A pigeon flies in and lands on a park railing.
expectation: It flares its wings to slow, extends its legs, grips the railing, and folds its wings; it does not stop dead in mid-air or land before reaching the rail.

caption: A child does a forward roll on a gym mat and comes up sitting.
expectation: She tucks her head and rolls over her back along the mat; her body stays whole and does not sink into the mat.

caption: A man pushes a broken-down car along a flat street while a friend steers, and the car slowly starts to roll.
expectation: He leans forward with straight arms against the car and drives with his legs; the car begins to move only after he pushes and only while he pushes.

caption: A boy ties the laces of his sneaker into a bow and pulls the loops tight.
expectation: The laces cross, loop, and pull through each other only where his fingers guide them; the knot tightens as he pulls and stays tied; the laces never pass through themselves or change length.

caption: A woman folds a bath towel in half and then in half again, and sets the folded square on a shelf.
expectation: The towel bends along the fold line and the halves lie flat on each other; the towel gets smaller and thicker with each fold; it does not stiffen, stretch, or fold on its own.

caption: A man crumples a sheet of paper into a tight ball in his fist and drops it on the desk.
expectation: The sheet wrinkles and folds in on itself as the fist closes; the ball keeps its crumpled shape and creases after release and does not unfold flat again.

caption: A hiker unfolds a paper map on the hood of a car and smooths it out with her hands.
expectation: The map opens along its existing creases and lies flat only where pressed, springing up slightly at the folds; it does not open by itself or change size.

caption: A woman rolls up a yoga mat from one end into a tight cylinder and stands it against the wall.
expectation: The roll grows thicker as more mat winds onto it; the layers sit on top of each other and do not pass through one another; the mat does not roll itself.

caption: A gardener coils a long garden hose into loops on the lawn.
expectation: Each loop lies on top of the last, the hose bends smoothly without kinking, and the length of hose on the ground shrinks as the coil grows; the hose does not pass through itself.

caption: A man shakes out a tablecloth and lets it settle over a dining table, and the edges hang down over the sides.
expectation: The cloth billows, then falls and drapes over the table top with the overhang hanging straight down under gravity; it does not float, stay rigid, or hang upward.

caption: A child folds a sheet of paper step by step into a paper airplane.
expectation: Each fold creases the paper where it is pressed and stays creased; the paper keeps its total area and does not gain or lose pieces; folds do not undo themselves.

caption: A camper pulls the drawstring of a cloth bag, and the bag's opening gathers shut.
expectation: The fabric around the opening bunches into gathers as the string is pulled through it; the opening closes only as the string tightens.

caption: A woman hangs a wet shirt on a clothesline by its shoulders, and the shirt hangs down and drips.
expectation: The shirt drapes straight down from the pegs, its wet fabric clinging and heavy; drips fall from the lowest edge; the shirt does not stand out stiffly or float.

caption: A man wraps a long scarf around his neck twice and tucks the end in.
expectation: The scarf bends around his neck in layers that lie on top of each other, and the free end gets shorter as it is wrapped; the scarf does not pass through itself or his neck.

caption: A sailor ties a knot in a thick rope and pulls both ends hard so the knot tightens.
expectation: The rope loops through itself only where his hands pass it, the knot shrinks and hardens as he pulls, and it holds; the rope does not stretch like elastic or merge with itself.

caption: A mover unrolls a rolled-up rug across a wooden floor with a push, and the rug lies flat.
expectation: The roll gets thinner as it travels and the unrolled part lies flat behind it; the roll slows and stops when the rug runs out; the rug does not roll back up.

caption: A woman folds a letter into thirds and slides it into an envelope.
expectation: The paper creases at the folds and becomes a smaller rectangle that fits into the envelope; the letter goes into the opening, not through the envelope's face.

caption: A child pulls a blanket off a bed and drags it across the floor behind her.
expectation: The blanket slides off the bed and trails on the floor in soft folds, following her path and bunching where it catches; it does not stay stiff or move ahead of her.

caption: A cashier tears a sheet of wrapping paper from a roll and folds it around a shoebox, creasing the corners.
expectation: The paper wraps around the box following its edges, creases where pressed, and the box's shape shows through; the paper does not stretch, shrink, or pass through the box.

caption: A ball rolls across a living-room floor, disappears behind a sofa, and comes out the other side.
expectation: The same ball reappears at the far side, at about the time and speed its motion behind the sofa implies; it does not emerge changed, doubled, or from the wrong side.

caption: A woman puts a set of keys into a small wooden box, closes the lid, then opens it again and takes the keys out.
expectation: The keys are hidden while the lid is shut and are the same keys when the lid opens; they do not vanish, change, or appear outside the box while it is closed.

caption: A man places an upturned cup over a coin on a table, slides the cup to the side, and lifts it to reveal the coin.
expectation: The coin is hidden under the cup and is found where the cup was slid to, having moved with it; the coin does not show through the cup or stay behind at the first spot.

caption: A woman walks along a street and passes behind a wide pillar, disappearing and then emerging on the far side.
expectation: She is hidden for a moment consistent with her walking pace and reappears at the same height and stride; her body does not show through the pillar or change while hidden.

caption: A cat climbs into a paper grocery bag on the floor, and the bag rustles and shifts as the cat moves inside it.
expectation: The bag bulges and moves where the cat pushes from inside; the cat's body does not show through the paper and the cat does not appear elsewhere while inside.

caption: A shopper drops three apples one by one into an empty cloth bag, and the bag sags and bulges.
expectation: The bag hangs lower and bulges more with each apple; the bulges match the apples' size and sit at the bottom; the apples do not fall through the cloth.

caption: A man pours a glass of water into an opaque metal jug, then tips the jug and pours the water back out into the glass.
expectation: About the same amount of water comes back out as went in; the water is unseen while in the jug and pours only from the spout.

caption: A toy car is pushed into one end of a cardboard tunnel and rolls out the other end.
expectation: The car exits after a delay matching its speed and the tunnel's length, moving in the same direction; the same car comes out and nothing exits before it enters.

caption: A man slides his arm into the sleeve of a coat and his hand emerges from the cuff.
expectation: The sleeve bulges and moves as the arm passes through; the hand appears at the cuff only after the arm has travelled the sleeve's length; the arm does not show through the fabric.

caption: A child hides behind a floor-length curtain, and the curtain bulges where she stands with her shoes showing beneath the hem.
expectation: The bulge matches her body and moves when she moves; only her shoes are visible below; she does not show through the fabric or appear elsewhere.

caption: A dog walks into its doghouse and a moment later pokes its head back out of the doorway.
expectation: The dog is out of sight while inside; its head comes out through the doorway only, not through the walls or roof; it is the same dog.

caption: A man tries to push a large hardcover book into a shoebox that is too small for it, and the book will not go in.
expectation: The book stops against the box's edges or bends the box outward; neither the book nor the box shrinks, and the book does not pass through the box's sides.

caption: A child drops a tennis ball into a bucket, then tips the bucket over and the ball rolls out onto the floor.
expectation: The ball is hidden inside the upright bucket and comes out only when the rim tilts low enough; it is the same ball and rolls away from the opening.

caption: A woman throws a blanket over a wooden chair, and the shape of the chair shows through the blanket.
expectation: The blanket settles onto the chair's back and seat and hangs down at the edges; the chair does not show through the fabric, and the blanket's bumps match the chair beneath.

caption: A car drives along a road, passes behind a parked truck, and reappears on the far side of it.
expectation: The car is hidden for a time consistent with its speed and the truck's length and emerges at the same speed and heading; it is the same car and does not show through the truck.

caption: A child pushes a coin into the slot of a piggy bank and then shakes the bank, and the coin rattles inside.
expectation: The coin disappears through the slot and stays inside; it does not fall out of the bank's solid sides or reappear outside; the bank's shape is unchanged.
